replies.author: MrNotmark
replies.body:
Three.js is better for quick scenes like this, demos and tech demos work well on three.js
For the AI it is easier to work with three.js because of the insane amount of knowledge that is online about it. But is it better at making games? Are those three.js games good even?
Probably not. Godot or a proper game engine will be miles ahead of theee.js they just need more work.

We used to talk about unreal vs godot/unity a lot back then. The consensus was always that you can build in godot quicker and it is more suitable for solo devs but unreal can create amazing and beautiful open world games, with godot that would be harder.
The same thing is true with three.js but now. Three.js is good if you develop with LLMs but it will hit a limit sooner, you can push godot further and unreal even further but those will require much more work. Unreal I would also not recommend for any solo devs it was made for AAA games honestly

My own testing has shown that AI agents actually works a lot better with three.js than Godot and Unreal. The existing game engines are somewhat clumsy for the AI agent to work with (although it can use them).

Especially Unreal comes with a lot of bling bling ready out of the box to get a cinematic look that you have to work harder to get with three.js, but it's not impossible.

comments.author: Glum-Drop-5724
comments.body:
> AI just makes it insanely easy to generate visually impressive Three.js demos, which is why you see so many of them. But they all feel awful to play and have 0 actual depth.

Is that due to an inherent limit within three.js, or just lack of effort and creativity on those who have used three.js for game development with AI so far?

replies.author: PrettyBaker2891
replies.body:
It's mostly a tooling and architecture problem, not an inherent limitation. 

You can build proper games with Three.js, but you're essentially building your own game engine on top of a rendering library. 

AI is also much better at generating impressive visuals than designing and implementing cohesive gameplay systems.

replies.author: tonios2
replies.body:
Everything you code and draw goes through JavaScript + Three.js and then the drawing abstraction WebGL or WebGPU if newer.
Theres just so many layers between your GPU and the actual draw command, and AI cant magically remove that.
So simple 3D games yes, but if you want latest graphics no.

replies.author: FailedGradAdmissions
replies.body:
No limitation, well there is a heavy performance limitation due to it being a library on top of a high level language on top of a browser… but setting that aside the real problem is it’s not a game engine.

Trying to utilize three.js to build you a game is no different from utilizing Vulkan or OpenGL. Again it’s merely a graphics library it’s not a game engine.

Somebody asking AI to build a game from scratch with three.js would be roughly equivalent to somebody asking you to make a cake and handing out to you raw wheat.
